clue.text: Placid old man racing competition to take on role of US president

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: taking something on means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the US president is CIC, commander-in-chief of the armed forces
Formula One, F1, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A calm elderly man running for office in some sort of race, as if stepping into the American presidency.
explanation.walkthrough: Formula One is written F1; the figure 1 is read as the letter I. The US president is commander-in-chief, abbreviated CIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacific is a dated synonym for peaceful or calm in temperament.

clue.text: Academic accepting nothing is watertight

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic
O, the zero shape, means nothing

explanation.surface: A lecturer who takes nothing on trust has an argument without holes.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, proof means resistant, as in waterproof, so impervious and watertight.

clue.text: Company moaning about nicknames

indicators.note: about here means in a jumble, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Colleagues grumbling about the names they're called at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognomina is the Latin plural of cognomen, a surname or descriptive extra name, so nicknames.

clue.text: Kelvin perhaps made nun flaunt it all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun was made to show off something wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: The kelvin, the SI unit of temperature, is one of the base units of measurement, an example.

clue.text: School accepting learner makes progress rather noisily

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: comp is short for comprehensive school, the UK state secondary school
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A school taking on a pupil whose progress is a bit loud.
explanation.definitionFit: To clomp is to walk with heavy, noisy steps.

clue.text: New sketch made by artist cutting coloured paper

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it, so one piece splits the other

parts.note: red is a colour, so coloured gives red
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist slicing up coloured paper to make a fresh sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is printed on pink paper, so 'coloured paper' reads naturally as one idea; here it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A redraft is a revised version of a drawing or document, a new draft.

clue.text: People coming back to provide one way to "see"

parts.note: to return is to yield or provide, as an investment returns a profit

indicators.note: one way to read see is the other way round, backwards

explanation.surface: Returning travellers offering one method of seeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one way to' asks for 'see' written in the reverse direction, EES.
explanation.definitionFit: Returnees are those who come back, for instance from abroad or from a spell away.

clue.text: Break dance one set up to occupy people

parts.note: a disco is a dance

indicators.note: occupying means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a nation is a people

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means raised, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a unit is one

explanation.surface: A dance where someone is installed among the people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses the word for one, giving TINU, before 'to occupy' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A discontinuation is a halt or interruption, a break in something.

clue.text: Brute that's somewhat lacking in soul

indicators.note: somewhat lacking means a little short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a brute is an animal, a beast

explanation.surface: A brute is a creature with little spirit inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology the anima is the inner self or soul.

clue.text: Tenth part of article about intercourse

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: the is the definite article
it is slang for sex

explanation.surface: A tenth of a magazine piece is about sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce or income paid to the church.

clue.text: Position in church organisation, high up, which deacon finally enters

parts.note: ORG is the standard abbreviation for organisation

indicators.note: entering something means going inside it, so a letter is placed within

parts.note: aloft means up high in the air

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word deacon

explanation.surface: A deacon takes up a lofty place in the church's hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts N, the end of 'deacon', inside ALOFT to give ANLOFT.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ loft is a raised gallery in a church where the organ and organist sit.

clue.text: Move screen round hospital

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped about the other

parts.note: to sift is to screen or sieve

explanation.surface: Wheeling a screen around a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift something is to move it from one place to another.

clue.text: Bits of alfalfa may be reduced to this vegetable matter

parts.words: Bits of alfalfa may be reduced to this
parts.note: every letter of the word alfalfa is ..., so split as ... the answer describes its bits

explanation.surface: Alfalfa crumbles away into plant matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is in reading the answer as 'F, L or A': those are the only letters alfalfa is built from.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora means plant life collectively, so vegetable matter in the botanical sense.

clue.text: Bore loudly interrupts harangue

indicators.note: interrupting something means breaking into it, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: to perorate is to speak at length, to harangue
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A dull person loudly breaking into someone's lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a noun for a tedious person; it is the verb to drill a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To perforate is to pierce or bore holes through something.

clue.text: Broadcast national fixture

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a Thai is a national of Thailand

explanation.surface: A national sporting fixture shown on television.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a match in a cup competition, a sporting fixture.

clue.text: One sentence following another repeatedly

parts.note: time is a prison sentence, as in doing time
after means following
another sentence, so time again

explanation.surface: A repeat offender handed one prison term after another.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning again and again, on many occasions.

clue.text: Part of car bonnet covered by packing

indicators.note: in a down clue, covered by means placed below, so the packing comes on top

parts.note: filler is material used for packing a space
a cap is a kind of bonnet or head covering

explanation.surface: Part of a car's bonnet is hidden under the packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bonnet' tempts as the car's hood; here it is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The filler cap closes the opening to a car's fuel tank.

clue.text: Young woman almost causing anxiety

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman
giving can mean causing, as in giving offence

explanation.surface: A girl who nearly brings on worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or apprehension.

clue.text: This falseness is not true

indicators.note: not true suggests letters that are out of line, so the phrase is rearranged

explanation.surface: A statement that is itself false, declaring its falseness untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of THIS FALSENESS, rearranged by 'not true', give the answer, and the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithlessness is disloyalty, being not true to someone, a kind of falseness.

clue.text: Not many said that's a relief

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: phew is the exclamation of relief

explanation.surface: Hardly anyone uttered words of relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Few means a small number, hardly any.

clue.text: Legitimacy forsaken by leader in appalling state

indicators.note: the word loses its leading letter

parts.note: lawfulness is legitimacy, being within the law

explanation.surface: Legitimacy abandoned by those in charge leaves a country in a dreadful condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forsaken by leader' drops the opening L of LAWFULNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Awfulness is the quality of being dreadful, an appalling condition.

clue.text: Unsociable ladies perhaps lining absolutely nothing up

indicators.note: lining means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other
up in a down clue means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: FA is short for sweet FA, British slang for nothing at all
the ladies is a women's toilet, an example of a loo

explanation.surface: Stand-offish women lining up for nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses FA to AF; 'sweet FA' is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and reserved, keeping apart from others.

clue.text: Large case of alcohol causing death

parts.note: fat means large, of great size

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A large crate of drink with deadly results.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatal means deadly, resulting in death.

clue.text: Stick man

definitions.meaning: a stick or rod, such as a walking pole
to provide people to work something, as in crewing a shop

explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a long stick, and to staff a place is to man it.

clue.text: Burning issue's beginning to fuel irrational fear

indicators.note: fuelling something means feeding into it, so a letter goes inside
irrational suggests disordered, so the letters are jumbled
beginning points to the first letter of issue

explanation.surface: The first spark of a burning issue feeds an unreasonable fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irrational' turns FEAR into AFRE, and 'to fuel' puts I, the first of 'issue's', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Afire means on fire, so burning, literally or with passion.

clue.text: Provide material for Beethoven duet

indicators.note: the letters are drawn from material inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Supplying music for a Beethoven piece for two.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or furnish someone with a quality.

clue.text: It's frequently made from revolutionary mesh

parts.note: of means made from, as in a ring of gold

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a net is a mesh

explanation.surface: Something often produced from mesh that has been turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Often is a straightforward synonym for frequently, many times.

clue.text: Card file I rearranged and cleared up

indicators.note: rearranged signals that the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An office worker reorganised a card index and tidied it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To clarify something is to clear up confusion about it, to make it plain.

clue.text: This might colour one's image having experienced upset

parts.note: felt is the past of feel, to experience
to tip is to upset or overturn

explanation.surface: A troubling experience might tinge how someone is seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colour one's image' suggests reputation, but the definition is literal: a pen for colouring pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tip pen is used to colour in drawings and pictures.

clue.text: Engineer cunningly providing turning at oblique angle

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: if means providing, on condition that

indicators.note: oblique means slanted or askew, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A designer builds a turning set at a slanting angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes FI from IF, and 'oblique' turns ANGLE into NAGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To finagle is to obtain or arrange by trickery, to wangle something craftily.
